gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Amazfit Bip Max costs $99.99 at Amazfit's US store, the same price as the Active 2 (Round), and claims up to 20 days of battery against the Active 2's 10. roxskin.io lists the Bip Max among Amazfit watches with HYROX Race mode but gives no price, so none of these results puts that watch at the same price with double the battery.
standout_why: I opened these pages. roxskin.io (cited in the third chat) names the Bip Max as a race-mode watch but gives no price or battery figure, and its under-$150 picks are only the Active 2 at about $100. Our own page (cited in all three chats) lists the Bip 6, Active 2 Round, PACE 3, FR165 and FR55, and never mentions the Bip Max or the Active 2 Square. ChatGPT's answers show the Active 2 Square at $112.37 at Walmart, which is not Amazfit's $149.99 price. They also say the PACE 3 is $199, but none of these results gives the $229 struck-through price COROS shows next to it. TechRadar did not render for me. wearablebeat.com returned 403 and roxgrit.com failed with a certificate error, so I can't rule out that they mention the Bip Max.
decides: The Amazfit lineup is still the answer under $150, and the Bip Max at $99.99 is a strong challenger to the Active 2 (Round) at the same price. Each runs Amazfit's HYROX Race mode, per Amazfit for the Active 2 and per roxskin.io for the Bip Max. The Bip Max claims twice the battery (20 days vs 10) and has a 2.07-inch screen against the Active 2's 1.32-inch one. The Active 2 keeps Single, Double and Team Relay race formats, which Amazfit lists for it. I found no source that lists those formats for the Bip Max. The Bip 6 at $79.99 stays the cheapest watch with race mode. Every COROS and Garmin watch here is over budget or has no price I could source. On top of that, none has a HYROX-named mode.
